From 9bdda4e9cf2dcecb60a0683b10ffb8cd7e5f2f45 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Amir Goldstein <amir73il@gmail.com>
Date: Sat, 1 Sep 2018 09:40:01 +0300
Subject: [PATCH] fsnotify: fix ignore mask logic in fsnotify()

Commit 92183a42898d ("fsnotify: fix ignore mask logic in
send_to_group()") acknoledges the use case of ignoring an event on
an inode mark, because of an ignore mask on a mount mark of the same
group (i.e. I want to get all events on this file, except for the events
that came from that mount).

This change depends on correctly merging the inode marks and mount marks
group lists, so that the mount mark ignore mask would be tested in
send_to_group(). Alas, the merging of the lists did not take into
account the case where event in question is not in the mask of any of
the mount marks.

To fix this, completely remove the tests for inode and mount event masks
from the lists merging code.

Fixes: 92183a42898d ("fsnotify: fix ignore mask logic in send_to_group")
Signed-off-by: Amir Goldstein <amir73il@gmail.com>
Signed-off-by: Jan Kara <jack@suse.cz>

diff --git a/fs/notify/fsnotify.c b/fs/notify/fsnotify.c
index f174397b63a0..ababdbfab537 100644
--- a/fs/notify/fsnotify.c
+++ b/fs/notify/fsnotify.c
@@ -351,16 +351,9 @@ int fsnotify(struct inode *to_tell, __u32 mask, const void *data, int data_is,
 
 	iter_info.srcu_idx = srcu_read_lock(&fsnotify_mark_srcu);
 
-	if ((mask & FS_MODIFY) ||
-	    (test_mask & to_tell->i_fsnotify_mask)) {
-		iter_info.marks[FSNOTIFY_OBJ_TYPE_INODE] =
-			fsnotify_first_mark(&to_tell->i_fsnotify_marks);
-	}
-
-	if (mnt && ((mask & FS_MODIFY) ||
-		    (test_mask & mnt->mnt_fsnotify_mask))) {
-		iter_info.marks[FSNOTIFY_OBJ_TYPE_INODE] =
-			fsnotify_first_mark(&to_tell->i_fsnotify_marks);
+	iter_info.marks[FSNOTIFY_OBJ_TYPE_INODE] =
+		fsnotify_first_mark(&to_tell->i_fsnotify_marks);
+	if (mnt) {
 		iter_info.marks[FSNOTIFY_OBJ_TYPE_VFSMOUNT] =
 			fsnotify_first_mark(&mnt->mnt_fsnotify_marks);
 	}
-- 
2.25.1

### Modifications in Each File

**File: `fs/notify/fsnotify.c`**
- Removed conditional checks for the inode and mount event masks when merging the lists of marks.
- The previous logic that checked if the event mask included `FS_MODIFY` or if the test mask matched the inode's or mount's fsnotify mask has been eliminated.
- The code now directly assigns the first inode mark to `iter_info.marks[FSNOTIFY_OBJ_TYPE_INODE]` without any conditions, ensuring that it always retrieves the first mark regardless of the mask.

### Relationships Between Modifications
The changes made in `fs/notify/fsnotify.c` are aimed at fixing the logic related to the ignore mask in the `fsnotify()` function. By removing the tests for the inode and mount event masks during the merging of the group lists, the patch ensures that the ignore mask on a mount mark is correctly applied to events from the same group. This modification is essential for the intended functionality of ignoring specific events while still allowing others, thus addressing the issue acknowledged in the previous commit (92183a42898d). The relationship is that the removal of the conditional checks directly supports the intended behavior of the ignore mask logic, leading to a more accurate event notification system.

```c

    !(test_mask & to_tell->i_fsnotify_mask) &&
```

```c
if ((mask & FS_MODIFY) ||
    (test_mask & to_tell->i_fsnotify_mask)) {
    iter_info.marks[FSNOTIFY_OBJ_TYPE_INODE] =
        fsnotify_first_mark(&to_tell->i_fsnotify_marks);
}
```
Reason:
The bug occurs because the merging logic for inode and mount marks does not account for the scenario where an event is not in the mask of any mount marks. This results in the ignore mask logic failing to function correctly, allowing events that should be ignored to be processed.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
```c
iter_info.marks[FSNOTIFY_OBJ_TYPE_INODE] =
    fsnotify_first_mark(&to_tell->i_fsnotify_marks);
```
```c
if (mnt) {
    iter_info.marks[FSNOTIFY_OBJ_TYPE_VFSMOUNT] =
        fsnotify_first_mark(&mnt->mnt_fsnotify_marks);
}
```
Reason:
The fix involves removing the conditional checks for the inode and mount event masks during the merging process. By directly assigning the first mark of the inode and mount marks to `iter_info.marks`, the code ensures that the ignore mask logic is applied correctly, allowing the system to properly handle events that should be ignored.
